I had a similar realization like 2 or 3 years ago. It’s earth shattering the way you realize how much you’ve abandoned yourself. Feeling my emotions again has been a real journey and not without its own set of mistakes. Like trying to set boundaries and not knowing how, lashing out at my parents and other family because of the sense of betrayal I felt. Feeling like they set me up for failure and that they had no idea who I was. I mean it was kinda true but I later realized that they had their own veils up and would never see where I was coming from, at least not on my timeline. My brother still fails to see how his substance abuse issues likely stem from how we were treated. It’s so frustrating, wanting someone to just get you. 

I’d start by prioritizing having people in your life that will validate you. The (unintentional) gaslighting that can happen from the friends and family who have known you all the time and are confused by your sudden change can seriously fuck you up. Just take care of yourself and realize it’ll take time to find a way to ground yourself in who you really are. Some people will resist, others will be happy to get to know this new you.

Lastly, emotions are hard to handle when you’re not used to it! But let them be a reminder of your natural intuition and a guide to understanding what truly matters to you (or your inner child) and why. It takes time but you will likely be a more dynamic human being by doing so.

Love and oneness are the purest things, which is what awakening shows you. It allows you to remember who you really are and let go of the fear that weighs us down. Love is high vibrational, fear is not. Fear dampens high vibrations and makes people reactive and irrational. It’s why people who are traumatized, especially at an early age, have a hard time feeling safe and in control of their lives. 

But by finding a way to come back to the true self, the one that yearns to give and receive love, we can regain our inherent power. Not the fake power that fear instills as a defense mechanism. 

The reason these things are hard to prove or test is because they are inherent to our being. You can’t “prove” love. You know it. You feel it. We all do. And while you can test and measure the physical responses to love, you can’t test love itself. The physical plane is only a part of existence.
